prompts.convex: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: ONE transparent pixel-art mine terrain transition corner, production game sprite. Reference image 1 is existing thin ContactDust A (preserve gritty muted stone palette and thin contact effect); reference 2 existing RockToe B; reference 3 existing Wall_RockMass (large faceted rocks STYLE). They are style references only, never redraw entire wall. Draw ONE convex OUTWARD L-shaped contact corner, wall occupies LOWER LEFT quadrant, floor occupies the other 3 quadrants. Imagine a 64x64 logical pixel canvas: vertex at (32,32), horizontal arm from (6,32) to (32,32) and vertical arm from (32,32) to (32,58). A thin irregular bedrock root follows that path; dark contact is immediately at wall side, low contrast mineral powder disperses outward above the horizontal arm and to the right of vertical arm, especially a natural convex diagonal shoulder northeast of the vertex. Keep corner center no darker than the arms. Complete small corner, not a disconnected pile. Partial olive-gray stone facet roots on wall-facing underside, sparse angular broken flakes merging into dust, NOT a row of pebbles. Near-black existing outline used only on tiny embedded roots. Max band width about 12 logical pixels, no giant boulders, no wall square, no floor backing. Pixel art crisp logical pixels, flat 3-5 tones in gray brown #747064 / cold gray #525E5E / dust #646153, restrained low contrast. No glow, no text, no border, no grid, no smooth blur or high resolution illustration. Actual transparent background and subtle stepped alpha at dusty outside. Center within square output with generous transparent margin; no part touches outside border. No characters. This is an overlay supplement placed beneath existing tiny stone rim, not a new wall.

STYLE REFERENCES: image1 original ContactDust A, image2 RockToe B, image3 Wall_RockMass. Match these existing assets, not a new style. NOT a full wall, no floor background, no tile board. Canonical corner has FLOOR only in UPPER RIGHT quadrant and rock wall in the other 3 quadrants. On imagined 64x64 logical pixels the concave vertex is (32,32): a vertical narrow root leg from (32,6) to (32,32), then horizontal leg from (32,32) to (58,32). Dust and broken mineral flakes lie inside that upper-right floor quadrant, to the right of the vertical leg and above the horizontal leg, gently filling the elbow without a dark overlapped square. Thin wall-side flat root fragments in gray-brown olive, cold blue gray contact shadows, sparse dusty #646153 and #747064 tiny clusters. Root fragments look like the lower portions of the existing LARGE wall facets, not a necklace of separate pebbles. Maximum transition width 10 logical pixels. Extremely subdued low contrast, no new obstacles. Crisp 1 logical pixel steps, only flat color clusters, stepwise semitransparency, no airbrush or blur. Preserve a natural thin asymmetric L silhouette. Genuine transparent outside and generous transparent margins. No characters, labels, text, frame, grid, lighting effects.
